entries.name: propbytes-propertycall-errored#0
entries.script: { sigmaProp(sigmaProp(true).propBytes.size > 0) }  // JVM: PARSES and then throws at eval: `propBytes` has a PerItemCost cost kind and no `propBytes_eval` handler, so MethodCall.eval takes the non-FixedCost branch and genericMethod.evalMethod raises RuntimeException("Cannot find eval method") — values.scala:1364-1390, SMethod.scala:138-159. sigma-rust has no SigmaProp method container at all and refuses this at PARSE instead, which shows up on the wire arm.

entries.name: isproven-propertycall-errored#1
entries.script: { sigmaProp(sigmaProp(true).isProven) }  // JVM: PARSES and then throws at eval: `isProven` has a cost kind of plain `null` and no `isProven_eval` handler, so MethodCall.eval takes the non-FixedCost branch and genericMethod.evalMethod raises RuntimeException("Cannot find eval method") — values.scala:1364-1390, SMethod.scala:138-159. sigma-rust has no SigmaProp method container at all and refuses this at PARSE instead, which shows up on the wire arm. The null cost kind still takes the `case _` branch — a type pattern does not match null — so this is the same missing-handler throw and not an NPE.

entries.name: propbytes-dedicated-node-accept#2
entries.script: { sigmaProp(sigmaProp(true).propBytes.size > 0) with propBytes as the DEDICATED node }  // JVM: the CONTROL — the same property reached through opcode 0xd0 (SigmaPropBytes) EVALUATES, to SigmaProp d3. So #0 is not about propBytes being unimplemented: it is the MethodCall encoding of it that cannot evaluate. A red here would mean the implementation lacks the node too, and #0/#1 would stop meaning anything.
